rules.title: Just cause requirement for residential tenancy termination after 12 months of occupancy
rules.effectiveDateQuote: This section shall become operative on April 1, 2024.
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential property for 12 months, the owner must not terminate the tenancy without just cause, which must be stated in the written notice. Just cause includes at-fault causes (default in rent, lease violations, nuisance, waste, criminal activity, illegal subletting, refusal of entry, unlawful use) and no-fault causes (owner or family intent to occupy for 12+ months, withdrawal from rental market, compliance with government habitability orders, intent to demolish or substantially remodel).
rules.quotedSpan: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.coverageDescription: Applies to all residential rental properties except: transient/tourist hotels, nonprofit hospital/religious facility housing, dormitories, housing where tenant shares kitchen/bathroom with owner, single-family owner-occupied residences renting no more than 2 units, 2-unit buildings where owner occupies one unit, housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome), certain individually-owned properties meeting ownership and notice requirements, and affordable housing restricted by deed or regulatory agreement.
exemptions: Housing in nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly, or adult residential facilities
Dormitories owned and operated by institutions of higher education or K-12 schools
Housing where tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with owner who maintains principal residence there
Single-family owner-occupied residences, including accessory dwelling units, renting no more than 2 units or bedrooms, or mobilehomes
2-unit buildings where owner occupied one unit as principal residence at tenancy start
Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes)
Individually-owned residential property not owned by a REIT, corporation, or certain LLCs, where tenants have received written notice of exemption
Affordable housing restricted by deed, regulatory agreement, or other recorded document, or subject to housing subsidy agreements
